title: Hark! from the Tombs a Doleful Sound
description: Hark! from the Tombs a Doleful Sound in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 63, headed “A funeral thought”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hark! from the tombs a dole-ful sound, My ears at-tend the cry, "Ye liv-ing men, come view the ground "Where you must short-ly lie.

lines: Hark! from the tombs a doleful sound,
"Ye living men, come view the ground
"Princes, this clay must be your bed,
"The tall, the wise, the reverend head
Great God, is this our certain doom?
Still walking downward to our tomb,
Grant us the powers of quickening grace
To fit our souls to fly,
Then, when we drop this dying flesh,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
